conventions.index: assets[id] is a flat index (props by id, skies by id, texture sets as texture:<set>, water textures as water:<name>) with files[] and the key data; the sky, textures, water and props sections hold the full detail.
conventions.units: Metres; glTF Y-up. Props face +Z where they have a front; pivot at the base centre unless the entry says otherwise.
conventions.props: Each prop file: root node <id> > [variant nodes] > lod0 [, lod1]. Show one LOD at a time. lod0/lod1 nodes (or their part children) carry the KHR_mesh_quantization dequantisation transform (a scale and offset): move, clone or hide them, but do not reset their local transforms. Variant nodes keep the source layout; to place one variant on its own, clone it and zero its position.
conventions.equirect: u = x / width from the left edge, v = y / height from the top. azimuthDeg = u * 360. elevationDeg = 90 - v * 180. three.js r187 (EquirectUV.js, HDRLoader flipY) maps world direction d to u = atan2(d.z, d.x) / 2pi + 0.5, so with no rotation d = (cos el cos t, sin el, cos el sin t), t = (u - 0.5) * 2pi: u = 0.25 is -Z, 0.5 is +X, 0.75 is +Z. sun.directionThree is that vector. To put the sun over the sea (-Z), set scene.backgroundRotation.y = scene.environmentRotation.y = sun.rotationYToPutSunAtNegZ and place the DirectionalLight at (0, sin el, -cos el) * distance. Derived from the three.js r187 source (backgroundRotation and environmentRotation are applied as the transposed rotation to the lookup direction; check.mjs verifies the numbers with three's own Matrix4/Euler). Caveat from the same source: with WebGPURenderer an equirect scene.background is sampled through PMREMNode, which also multiplies by materialEnvRotation, and for the background mesh that resolves to scene.environmentRotation whenever scene.environment is set. So with both set, the visible sky may turn twice; if it does, set only environmentRotation.y. Confirm once at look-dev.
conventions.skyIntensity: HDR values are as shipped by Poly Haven (relative, not absolute: the night HDRI is exposed up). sun.intensity is the irradiance of the removed sun disc in the same units, so with environmentIntensity = k use DirectionalLight intensity = k * sun.intensity and colour sun.colorLinear. Pick per-mood intensities at look-dev.
conventions.layers: Cloud and star layers cover the upper hemisphere only: 4096 x 1024, row 0 = zenith, last row = horizon, same u as their HDRI. sRGB WebP; linear HDR radiance = srgbToLinear(texel.rgb) * hdrScale. Clouds: straight (not premultiplied) alpha.
conventions.textures: albedo sRGB; normal OpenGL (+Y up); orm linear R occlusion, G roughness, B metalness. sizeM is the real-world size one texture repeat covers: UV scale = metres / sizeM.

sand_dry.sizeSource: estimate: ambientCG publishes no dimensions for Ground093C; set from the scale of the wind-eroded ripples
sand_dry.why: Chosen over Poly Haven coast_sand_01: Ground093C is the warm cream sand of the palette, while coast_sand_01 is brown and gravelly with debris.

colorSpace.orm: linear; R occlusion, G roughness, B metalness

sand_wet.why: Source albedo is very dark (mean linear 0.11) and reads olive-grey next to sand_dry; it is scaled per channel to sand_dry's mean colour x 0.4 (wet sand is roughly 40-50% as bright as the same sand dry), keeping its variation, so the shoreline blends from dry to wet without a hue jump. Remove `calibrate` in config.json to get the source colours back.
